items: `template/src/pdca_harness/flow.py:2716` and `template/src/pdca_harness/cli.py:696`: the patch adds a reason the brief did not ask for, `"unchecked"`. If the end-of-run check itself fails (for example, its fetch fails twice), every carried bundle is marked `"unchecked"` and the run exits 1, even though every bundle is COMPLETE and no rewrite was seen. This fails closed and fits the invariant ("never ends reporting success while…"), but it also means a network hiccup after a fully successful run now turns exit 0 into exit 1. The other choice is a warning on stderr with exit 0 or 3. A human should decide which is wanted, since automation reads this exit code.

**The prerequisite the criterion needs doesn't exist yet.** `dependency-state.json` lists `693` as `"state": "PLANNED"`, so it is not built and not merged. The brief says it is "Verified against … `origin/main` @ `d6057eb`" and sets `Repo + branch target: eduralph/pdca-harness @ main`. But criterion (1) reads the exit code "the way bundle 693's test reads it … or `_drive_and_act`'s return passed through the CLI's own exit-code function". On main, `_drive_and_act` returns only the `results` state map (`flow.py:2562,2573`), and `cli._flow` (`cli.py:562-578`) has no run-level outcome path. The brief can't name the API it tells Do to extend ("whatever run-level signal bundle 693 added", Citations line), so Do starts from an unknown base, or on main with no exit-1 path at all. Either pin this bundle to 693's branch/API once it lands, or restate (1) so it doesn't depend on 693.

**"A rewrite outranks a hold (exit 3, from 693)" is a requirement with no test.** None of criteria (1)–(5) runs a hold and a late rewrite together. The exit-3 value and its precedence come from 693, which is unbuilt. The thread doesn't ask for exit 1 either: issue #695 says "report a rewrite as a hold or stop". Either add a criterion that pins the precedence (a run with one `held_conflict` and one late rewrite exits 1), or drop the line.

**The criterion doesn't test the issue's own "Done when" window.** The issue says: "A carried branch rewritten **during the last fold** is reported by the run that folded it." Criterion (1) only rewrites `fix/A` "while wave 1 (the last) builds", which is after the last fold has pushed. Nothing pins a rewrite between `_carried_tips` reading the tip (`integrate.py:591`) and the push (`:553`). The design probably covers it, because `carried.update(took)` at `:563` records the checked tip and the end check compares against that. Still, the issue's literal case goes untested. Add a variant that injects the force-push from an `integrate._git` spy on the `push` call of the last fold.

**The stated invariant is broader than the scope.** "Invariant to restore: A run never ends reporting success while its integration line carries commits that a branch it carried no longer holds, whenever the rewrite happened during the run." The scope says "a branch that no longer resolves is left alone", and criterion (2) requires "merged and deleted … reports nothing". In-fold, a gone branch is not just skipped: `_gone_branch` checks the PR's merged head against the base (docs `07-crosscutting.md:675-680`). The end check would do no such judgment. So a carried branch whose PR is closed unmerged, or squash-merged, and then deleted after the last fold leaves the line holding commits no PR holds, and the run still exits 0. Either narrow the invariant to "rewritten, still-resolving branches", or bring `_gone_branch`'s judgment into the end check. The two can't both stay as written.

**The brief points at "Known limits" text that isn't there.** Scope says: "Update the #633 'Known limits' text where it lives (`docs/07-crosscutting.md:668-675` and the `integrate.py` module docstring, `:38-44`)." Neither range lists these limits. `docs:669-675` and `integrate.py:39-45` describe #633's working behaviour ("the next fold stops the run"). The only "Known limits" in that doc section is at `docs:734-741`, and it is about the #646 carry, not #633. The issue quotes the limits from PR #685's description (`results/issue_633/pr-description.md:101-104`), not from repo text. Do will either invent a "Known limits" paragraph or edit the behaviour description without knowing which. Say what to change instead: extend the "next fold stops the run" sentences to cover the end of the run and the retried fetch.

**When the end-of-run check runs, and whether it duplicates the in-fold report, is left open.** Scope says "Only where folds ran". A run that broke out at `flow.py:2539-2544` (a fold raised, possibly `_carried_tips`' own rewrite error) or at the re-gate stop (`:2555-2559`) can still have a non-empty `carried_heads`. As written, the check would then print a second rewrite report for a branch the fold already reported, which breaks "stderr has one line that names `issue_A`". Say whether the check runs after a `break`, and add a no-duplicate case.

**Act runs before the planned report location.** The brief puts the new report beside `_warn_stranded_split_children` / `_report_conflict_holds` (`flow.py:2570-2572`), but `_maybe_run_act` runs first at `:2564-2565`, with `any_complete` computed from states that the late rewrite doesn't change. That fits the brief's "while … Act runs" window. It also means Act's review sees a run that looks clean, and the check can't block anything Act does. If that is intended, say so in the brief. Otherwise run the check before Act and run Act anyway. Either way, decide it before Do starts.
